✗ Digital wellbeing & balance

We optimize what we can measure. We have simply never built the measurement layer for the dimension that may matter most: the balance between who a child is online and who they are becoming offline.

? Missing
There is no compass to guide us through the health of our online and offline engagement.
Apps and products exist to count screen time and block content. None address the quality of online engagement or how to channel it toward better content, or more importantly, real-life interactions. Balance builds this.
Problem

Children are most vulnerable to this exposure. Digital parenting is hard.

7+ hours on a screen is not a leisure choice. It is algorithmic exposure: content engineered to hold attention at the expense of development. The effects show up in depression rates, sleep studies, and pediatric anxiety referrals climbing every year.

From our parent interviews

"I have no idea what my kid is actually watching, or what it's doing to them. I don't even know how to start that conversation. I know more outdoor time is better — every parent does. But knowing that and actually driving that change? That's a different thing entirely."

— Parent of a 12-year-old · Research interview, June 2026
Problem

Recommendation platforms are winning.

Engineered with billions of investment to capture attention. Minors have no defence.

7.5 hrsAverage daily screen time for kids 8–18
$11BEarned annually from minors' attention
The Impact

It affects all of us, but minors bear the highest cost.

Children and teens are uniquely vulnerable: still developing impulse control, social identity, and emotional regulation.

2×Higher depression risk with 3+ hrs/day social media
1 in 3US adolescents reporting persistent sadness
Our focus Children bear the greatest risk. Balance gives parents a clear window into their child's digital habits — and the tools to encourage healthier choices, online and off.
Product

Understand & incentivize better online and offline behavior. Not report and block.

Balance surfaces what children actually watch and scores their engagement, then gives families the tools & awareness to build better habits, together.

Balance Score

The AAP 5Cs Framework is built into the Balance Score

The Balance Score isn't an arbitrary metric — it's grounded in the American Academy of Pediatrics' clinical guidelines for healthy child development, ensuring every recommendation is backed by research, not guesswork.
